metrics.failurePrecision: matched reviewed failed targets / all emitted failed targets; report numerator and denominator, never a zero-denominator percentage
metrics.caseCoverage: browser cases executed through both public processes / all reviewed browser cases
metrics.abstention: count reviewed acquisition cantTell/untested annotations and rule inapplicable/cantTell/untested outcomes separately
metrics.falsePositives: emitted failed targets not present in the corresponding reviewed rule oracle
metrics.mutationKillRate: reviewed rule-eligible mutations producing the named failure / all reviewed rule-eligible mutations; acquisition-only mutations are reported separately
limitations: The nineteen public cases belong to one fictional application family and are visible during development.
Three reviewed bounds failures are too small a denominator for a real-world precision estimate.
Acquisition-only clipping, occlusion, overflow, peer-size, transformed-text, and direction cases do not gain rule verdicts without explicit applicability and policy.
Complete hit regions and pixel-content identity remain cantTell.
No private holdout or independent dual review exists.

cases.falsePositiveRisk: Inferring peer intent from repeated pixels or unequal gaps would manufacture an unsupported failure.
cases.nonClaim: A zero exit code does not prove the ambiguous layout has good UX; it means no current deterministic rule has sufficient evidence to fail it.

review.rationale: The correct rule behavior is abstention through inapplicability because no peer relation is emitted.

cases.falsePositiveRisk: Viewport bounds must not be substituted for document bounds, or legitimate below-the-fold content would fail.
cases.nonClaim: Passing existing kernel rules is not a general visual-quality or UX judgment.

review.rationale: All captured node render boxes remain within the document canvas; peer spacing is not evaluated without a relation.

cases.falsePositiveRisk: Promoting rectangular ancestor clipping directly into a failure would ignore intentional carousels, masks, and reveal interactions.
cases.nonClaim: The adapter detects one acquisition conflict; no current rule determines whether this clipped content is harmful.

review.rationale: Existing rules receive exact core geometry only and do not infer a clipping policy from the private Web extension.

cases.falsePositiveRisk: Treating a visual child rectangle as the complete hit target, or treating a disabled/hidden control as a geometry defect, would create unsupported failures.
cases.nonClaim: This case demonstrates separable native evidence and center samples, not touch-target conformance.

review.rationale: All selected control geometry remains within the document and no exact hit region is asserted.

cases.falsePositiveRisk: A visibility-aware future policy must distinguish intentionally parked controls; the current exact bounds rule only proves the render box is outside the document.
cases.nonClaim: The one bounds failure does not prove why the control moved or establish general interaction quality.

review.rationale: The source mutation moves the enabled export control beyond the document's left edge, which is sufficient for the existing exact bounds rule.

cases.falsePositiveRisk: Treating the adjacent complementary promotion as a metric peer would create a false-positive spacing verdict.
cases.nonClaim: The hard negative establishes one protected valid asymmetry, not broad precision across real websites.

review.rationale: Native hierarchy and complementary semantics are preserved, while no peer relation is invented.

cases.falsePositiveRisk: A geometry-only overlap rule could falsely fail valid dialogs and popovers without source intent, role, and interaction-state evidence.
cases.nonClaim: Zero failures protects one declared overlay example and is not broad overlay precision evidence.

review.rationale: The selected dialog is source-declared intentional, remains within document bounds, and does not create a supported current-rule failure.

cases.falsePositiveRisk: Using the screenshot viewport as the core canvas would falsely fail valid below-the-fold nodes.
cases.nonClaim: Viewport extent coverage records what was captured; it does not label below-the-fold content as a UI defect.

review.rationale: The document canvas contains the responsive page even though one viewport screenshot is partial.

cases.falsePositiveRisk: Conflating below-fold document content with screenshot absence would fail a valid page even though this selected baseline is positioned in the captured viewport.
cases.nonClaim: The clean baseline proves only the reviewed acquisition facts and existing rule behavior.

review.rationale: The notification baseline has no overflow, clipping, transform conflict, or out-of-document geometry.

cases.falsePositiveRisk: Failing every center occlusion could misclassify transient or intentional layers; issue #24 must define sufficient evidence and applicability.
cases.nonClaim: The adapter detects the sampled blocker, but the current kernel makes no occlusion verdict.

review.rationale: The acquisition oracle records the changed center-hit evidence while the rule oracle conservatively remains inapplicable.

cases.falsePositiveRisk: A center hit is only one sample and must not be generalized into a fully usable hit rectangle.
cases.nonClaim: The unobstructed sample does not establish complete interaction accessibility.

review.rationale: The selected action's center resolves to the action while all core geometry remains in bounds.

cases.falsePositiveRisk: A viewport-only canvas or rounded transform delta could change the failure target; the oracle requires document-space exact render evidence.
cases.nonClaim: The mutation kill proves one bounds path, not general browser acquisition accuracy or UX severity.

review.rationale: The targeted transform moves only the selected card's render box beyond the document's left edge.

cases.falsePositiveRisk: Scroll/client overflow alone cannot distinguish harmful truncation from intentional ellipsis with an alternate disclosure path.
cases.nonClaim: The measured overflow does not establish that the user cannot recover the full text.

review.rationale: No current deterministic rule consumes private Web overflow evidence, so the mutation is acquisition-only.

cases.falsePositiveRisk: Repeated-card appearance must not be upgraded into semantic peer membership solely to produce a size-consistency failure.
cases.nonClaim: Unequal measured heights are not themselves proof of a UI defect.

review.rationale: The adapter preserves the dimensions but emits no exact peer relation required by a consistency rule.

cases.falsePositiveRisk: Using desktop expectations for the mobile layout could produce the wrong target; the oracle requires the mobile document-space render box.
cases.nonClaim: The failure kills one mobile bounds mutation, not responsive-design quality in general.

review.rationale: At the declared mobile viewport, only the transformed revenue card crosses the document's left edge.

cases.falsePositiveRisk: Assuming left-to-right or horizontal writing when interpreting geometry could create direction-dependent false positives.
cases.nonClaim: Passing current rules does not establish RTL localization or reading-order quality.

review.rationale: Native direction and writing-mode evidence is retained while no direction-specific rule is admitted.

cases.falsePositiveRisk: A geometry-only adapter must not upgrade visual similarity into exact peer membership just to kill the spacing mutation.
cases.nonClaim: The adapter measures the 16 CSS-pixel transform but protocol 0.1 deliberately does not prove the corresponding spacing defect.

review.rationale: Acquisition truth records the transform conflict separately from the unavailable peer relation required by the rule.

cases.falsePositiveRisk: Reusing unscaled geometry or assuming increased document height is a defect would create false failures.
cases.nonClaim: This case proves capture at one declared text scale only; it does not establish accessibility conformance.

review.rationale: Scaled native geometry remains within the document canvas, and no peer relation is emitted.

cases.falsePositiveRisk: Using computed font size alone could miss rendered scaling, while treating every transform as harmful could fail legitimate emphasis or animation.
cases.nonClaim: The layout/render conflict is acquisition evidence, not a small-text conformance result.

review.rationale: No current rule has visible-ink evidence or a transformed-text policy, so the correct present behavior is non-failure.
